reports.title: Csquare Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Business Highlights

guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance Summary
section: For the full year 2026, Csquare expects total revenues between $1.14 and $1.16 billion, Adjusted EBITDA between $490 and $500 million, recurring capital expenditures between $50 and $60 million, and non-recurring growth capital expenditures between $620 and $640 million.

Metric | Updated 2026 Outlook | Prior Outlook
Total Revenue | $1,140 – $1,160 million | $1,130 – $1,170 million
Adjusted EBITDA | $490 – $500 million | $460 – $480 million
Recurring Capital Expenditures | $50 - $60 million | $55 - $65 million
Growth Capital Expenditures | $620 - $640 million | $610 - $660 million

desk.headline: Revenue up 26% to $302m, beat; loss widened on IPO costs; 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook raised to $490-500m
results: Revenue rose 25.6% to $302.3m, ahead of the $289m estimate; colocation revenue grew 26.7% while interconnection fell 7%.
The net loss widened to $88.1m ($0.58 a share) from $29.8m, driven by $58.6m of IPO-related deal and pay costs and higher interest.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 44% to $132.1m, and its margin widened to 47.8% from 40.5%.
Record bookings of $66.1m; customers have contracted 428 MW against 397 MW of sellable capacity, with about $114m of signed revenue still to start.
July IPO proceeds of about $1.16bn were used to repay roughly $1.1bn of debt; growth capex in the quarter was $149m.

guidance.summary: Csquare raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA outlook to $490-500m (was $460-480m) and narrowed its revenue range to $1.14-1.16bn, with the same midpoint. Recurring and growth capex ranges were trimmed.

watch: Whether new capacity comes online fast enough to serve contracted demand above 100% of sellable power.
Interest costs and FFO now that IPO proceeds have cut debt.
Whether IPO-related costs fade from the net loss in Q4.
